answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable stake: every identity must lock scarce collateral and collect vouchers from already-staked peers before it may trade. Like a glacier leaving shale at an inlet, each new account leaves a visible, expensive trail. A hacker who fabricates a thousand agents must fund a thousand bonds and forfeits every one when the ring is detected, so the cost grows with the fraud while fake names alone buy nothing.
